div.head: Duns 6.2
div.ab: Sic omnis qui cooperans uel conscius sit, ubi unlandiscus homo inlandiscum derie (id est extraneus indigenam noceat), adlegiet se super conscientia illa secundum precium captalis; et hoc iusiurando electo, quod dicitur cyreað. Et qui eum impetit, inducat causam suam mid foraðe (id est cum preiuratione).
Swa eac ælc ðe gewita oððe gewyrhta sy, ðær utlendisc man inlendiscan derie, geladie ðære midwiste be ðes orfes weorðe; ⁊ þæt sy cyreað; ⁊ se ðe hyne belecge, ofga his spræce mid foraðe.

Let every one that is cognisant or complicit where a stranger injures a native clear himself of such complicity [by an oath] to the value of the [lost] livestock, and [that oath] is to be a select oath [cyre-a‏‏þ]; and he who accuses him shall begin his case with a foreoath.

So auch jeder [andere], der [als] Mitwisser oder Beihelfer [verklagt] ist, wo ein ausländischer Mann einen inländischen schädigt, reinige sich von solcher Mitwissenschaft [durch Eid] in Höhe des [verlorenen] Viehwerthes; und dies sei ein Eid mit [vom Gegner] ernannten [Helfern]; und wer ihn beschuldigt, beginne seine Klage durch Klage-Eid.

So also let everyone [else] who [is accused as] accessory or helper, where a foreign man harms a native, clear himself of such complicity [by oath] to the value of the [lost] cattle; and let this be an oath with [helpers] nominated [by the opponent]; and let whoever accuses him begin his suit with a fore-oath.
div.note: K: ‘cooperaus’ corrected to ‘cooperans’ (a misreading); spacing tidied. Liebermann compares II As 1.1 and 23.2.
